title: Cohort alignment drift causing slot evaporation and prolonged batch waits
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed repeated tail-latency spikes across several production pools caused by extended batch formation times. The immediate symptom was a set of requests waiting for >150ms in the batch window before being sent to the GPU, producing 95th+ latency regressions and request reordering for priority tiers. Impact: intermittent degraded response times for hosted API customers and a handful of customer-facing timeouts during a high-traffic period. Detection: alerting from the perf-dashboard (batch-window-duration > 120ms) and multiple SLO breach warnings. Root cause (engineer summary): an interaction between a scheduler epoch change (timer granularity regressed to 20ms in runtime-1.19), a recent priority-mapping refactor that reduced early-fill incentives for low-priority cohorts, and a subtle race where batch slots in the cohort ring were treated as "evaporated" when the local slot owner missed a heartbeat. This produced cohort size skew and persistent micro-gaps (slot evaporation) which prevented the continuous coalescer from forming balanced batches. The coalescer continued waiting for phantom slots, causing prolonged waits for active requests while other pools produced suboptimal tiny batches. The issue was reproducible under bursty request patterns and worsened when autoscaling churned worker assignments. Immediate mitigation: 1) rolled back the priority-mapping change in runtime-1.19 to restore early-fill incentives for low-priority cohorts; 2) temporarily lowered batch-window max to 80ms for affected pools; 3) added a fast-path that treats missing heartbeat slots as dead after 2 ticks to break waiting loops. Permanent remediation plan (high level): - Harden scheduler heartbeat semantics and add monotonic epoch checks to prevent false slot evaporation. - Reintroduce adaptive early-fill bonus for cohorts with historically small sizes. - Add coordinator-level quorum checks to prevent a single worker's missed timer from blocking cohort formation. - Improve observability (new metrics and dashboards) to detect cohort skew and slot evaporation early. Action items: 1) implement epoch monotonicity guard and heartbeat reconciliation (owner: Ravi, est 3 pts) 2) rework priority-mapping with simulation harness for cohort fairness (owner: Priya, est 5 pts) 3) dashboard and alerts for cohort_skew_ratio and evaporated_slots (owner: Lin, est 2 pts) 4) run long-duration chaos test against autoscaler churn to validate fixes (owner: SRE team, est 3 pts). Links: perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference/prod/batching; incident runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-100401; rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1264; heartbeat fast-path PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2138. Postmortem goal: produce a blameless incident report and land all remediation in runtime-1.19.1 with validated simulations and new alerting.
